chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Verily the comfort, the rest, the success, the assistance, the achievement, the blessing, the benevolence, the forgiveness, the well-being, the ease, the glad tidings, the Divine pleasure, the nearness, the help, the empowerment, the hope, and the love from Allah — Mighty and Majestic — are for whoever befriends Ali and takes him as Imam, and disavows his enemies, and submits to his merits and to the successors after him.

It is a right upon me that I include them in my intercession, and a right upon my Lord — Blessed and Exalted — that He answers me regarding them. For they are my followers, and whoever follows me is indeed from me.

key_terms.ائْتَمَّ بِهِ: To take him as Imam — to follow his religious and spiritual leadership
key_terms.الرِّضْوَانُ: Ridwan — Divine pleasure/approval, the highest reward in Islamic theology
key_terms.الْفَلْجُ: Falj — success or triumph (an archaic classical Arabic term rarely seen in later literature)
key_terms.بَرِئَ مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ: Tabbara/bara'a — ritual and doctrinal dissociation from the enemies of Ali
key_terms.تَوَلَّى عَلِيّاً: To accept Ali's wilayah — friendship, loyalty, and recognition of his divine authority
key_terms.شَفَاعَتِي: Intercession (shafa'ah) — the Imam's role as intercessor on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What spiritual rewards does Imam al-Baqir promise to followers of Ali and the Imams in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) enumerates seventeen divine gifts — including comfort, success, forgiveness, and love from God — that are granted to those who accept the wilayah (guardianship) of Imam Ali and his successors, disavow his enemies, and acknowledge his merits. The Imam then declares that such devoted followers have a right upon his intercession, and he himself has a right upon God to accept his intercession for them. The hadith closes with the powerful prophetic echo: 'whoever follows me is from me.' This teaching was directed to Shia communities in the early Abbasid period who needed theological grounding and assurance of salvation through devotion to the Imams.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Hassan Bin Ziyad, from al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The comfort, and the rest, and the success, and the Assistance, and the achievement, and the Blessings, and the Benevolence, and the Forgiveness, and the healing, and the ease, and the Glad Tidings, and the (Divine) Pleasure, and the nearness, and the Help, and the competence, and the hope, and the Love from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is for the one who befriends Ali<sup>asws</sup> and makes him<sup>asws</sup> as an Imam<sup>asws</sup> with him<sup>asws</sup>, and disavows from his<sup>asws</sup> enemies, and submits to his<sup>asws</sup> merits, and to the successors<sup>asws</sup> from after him<sup>asws</sup>, would have a right upon me<sup>asws</sup> than I<sup>asws</sup> include him<sup>asws</sup> in my<sup>asws</sup> intercession, and he would have a right upon my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High that He<sup>azwj</sup> Answers me<sup>asws</sup> regarding them, for they would be my<sup>asws</sup> followers, and the one who follows me<sup>asws</sup>, so he is from me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Fadala ibn Ayyub from al-Hassan ibn Ziyad from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said that abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said the following. “

Tranquillity, comfort, victory, support, success, blessings, honor, forgiveness, relief, ease, glad news, satisfaction, nearness, triumph, capabilities, hope and love from Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, are for those who love (acknowledge the Divine authority of) Ali (a.s.) and follow him, disavows the enemies of Ali (a.s.) and accept in submission the virtues of Ali and his successors after him.

I am obligated to include them in my task of intervention on their behalf. It will be a truth before my Lord, the Most Holy, the Most High, to approve my intervention on their behalf. They are my followers and those who would follow me they will be of me.” 1. In M`r’atu ’I- ’ uqul (vol. 2, p.425) al- Aliamah al-Majlisi has pointed out that this phrase has been omitted, and that the reason for this becomes evident at the end of the hadith.
